premise: I spent 15 years paying $72,000 in premiums on my mother’s long-term-care policy, naming myself sole beneficiary to cover her nursing home, but when she died my sister-in-law at the insurance brokerage forged a beneficiary change and collected the $180,000 death benefit; I uncovered the original signed policy tucked in my mother’s Bible, proved the forgery, won the payout plus punitive damages, and now run “Policy of Deceit Advocacy,” where my sister-in-law answers phones in a headset that broadcasts her fraud case number and her garnished wages fund free elder-law clinics.
